chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act I
chapter.title: The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi Katheryne, we heard that you have a new commission for us?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: That's correct. There's a requester who has submitted a designated commission for the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A designated commission? Sounds like it must be pretty important. Uh, what kind of task is it, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hehe, there's no need to worry. This commission is not dangerous by any means. Perhaps you have heard that Inazuma will soon be holding a major festival — the "Magnificent Irodori Festival."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! A festival! Come to think of it, we haven't attended a festival in Inazuma for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The Yashiro Commission and Lady Yae are responsible for all the festival preparations. The one who has requested your help is none other than Lady Yae herself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, so it's Miko's commission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you know Miko... She always has some unusual ideas in her head. You can bet a festival planned by her is gonna be one to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'd better go to Grand Narukami Shrine and see what she needs us to do.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Lady Yae is currently at Yae Publishing House in Hanamizaka, so there's no need to go all the way to the shrine. In fact, she has instructed me to have you directly meet with her there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, well that's convenient enough. Let's go then!

talks.objective: Go to Yae Publishing House to look for Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Aratani and Kuroda, how are things coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: All the books and commissioned prints for Yae Publishing House were bound and sent out yesterday afternoon, Lady Yae.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Very good. And Murata?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: We have already received word from Eipekkusu and Sailing Breeze that the materials are all in place for "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power" and "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?"!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well done. And what about you, Onodera?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ahem. O—no—de—ra?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, yes Lady Yae! Everything is ready for the new issue release party.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You are the one who organized the plans for this release party. In other words, you are the team's fearless leader now. So please, show some confidence.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Besides, there's no need to be nervous. This project is destined for success, I feel quite optimistic about it.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I shall specially grant you leave for the next couple of days, Onodera. Please take the opportunity to have a good rest. After all, you will be very busy on the day of the release party.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Yes, Lady Yae. Thank you very much!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Alright then, is everyone clear about their assignments? Good. We are running out of time, so let's get moving! Chop chop!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, hello little ones. I take it you have received my commission, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some organizer you are! It's nearly time for the festival and you're still over here ramping things up for your light novel business! Shouldn't you be getting back to the Grand Narukami Shrine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You weren't thinking of dumping all the festival preparations on us, were you? Hmph, if so, then you can forget it, Paimon won't accept such a commission!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, forget it!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: My my, such harsh words... It hurts to hear that kind of talk from you two. But, as you can clearly see, I'm here working like a dog for the festival, yet you say I'm not doing my job.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Let me ask you, little ones, who ever said that the festival must involve the Grand Narukami Shrine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But isn't that a given? This is Inazuma, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Yes, that is true. But now that the Sakoku Decree has been lifted, Inazuma is no longer the same nation that once resisted change tooth and nail.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Therefore, rather than sticking to the same old traditional festival, the Yashiro Commission and I have decided to shake things up a little... This time, we'll be holding an international cultural festival, distinctly Inazuman but with a unique twist.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, I suppose I should start by telling you the origins of the Irodori Festival.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Legend has it that there were five poets in ancient Inazuma who were supremely gifted in singing and writing poetry. They are known as "The Five Kasen."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Every year, one of the five would present a collection of the group's poems to the Shogun for review, which would then spark cultured discussions regarding those works.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Thanks to them, Inazuma's culture blossomed and gained great influence at that time.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As time passed, people began creating various tales based on The Five Kasen. The Irodori Festival was also developed as a result to show appreciation for their works which so greatly enriched our lives.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a festival that's really rooted in culture.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Indeed, to describe it in the words of the ancients, it'd be "refined elegance." Unfortunately, with the flow of time, people have gradually forgotten about The Five Kasen and the festival.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Which is precisely why I've decided to revive the Irodori Festival by...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Holding a cultural convention featuring light novels!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wa—Wait a minute... light novels!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about all that "refined elegance" stuff you just said?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Please stop looking at me with those baffled expressions. In ancient times, poetry was all the rage. But nowadays, the entertainment format of choice is light novels.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The important thing is not the format but the creative work itself. It is impossible to come up with anything fresh if you're stuck using some rigid format of the past.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Speaking of which, don't you think that the concept of "focusing on the now" perfectly suits the current Inazuma?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And besides, it's a great opportunity to reintroduce Inazuma to all Teyvat through light novels. As they say, it's two birds with one stone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that was close... Paimon was nearly carried away by Miko's persuasive tongue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon Miko, you can't fool us! We know you by now, this is all definitely stemming from your own personal interests!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Haha, I can't deny that my hobbies had no part to play in this. However, regardless of whether it's light novels or a festival, catching people's attention with a fresh concept is the essence here.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well, what do you say? Aren't you two even a little curious about what interesting things you might see at the festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, maybe a little... Ah alright, Paimon's super curious now!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe. Come, let's pay a visit to the venue in Ritou together. I promise that it will give you a whole new perspective on the festival.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: There we'll meet a special someone who will tell you more about your tasks.

choices.text: A whole lot of thinly veiled self-justifications?

talks.objective: Go to the Irodori Festival site on Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: During the Irodori Festival, the area around the Outlander Affairs Agency will become the main exhibition space for light novels.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Once things are in full swing, not only will there be lots of official and fan-created work on display, there'll also be exclusive giveaways, prizes, and new release parties.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: This small plaza in front of the International Trade Association will be called "The Five Kasen Plaza" during the festival, and nearby shops will be selling special light novel merchandise. You certainly won't want to miss out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, how should Paimon put this... It's definitely not your typical festival, but it sure looks like it'll be quite the party!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's like a light novel paradise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, Miko, what are these blank boards in the center of the plaza?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Yes, those are—

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ah, Lady Yae did mention that there would be some reliable helpers coming to assist with the festivities. It appears she meant you two.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: At last, we meet again, Traveler and Paimon. Tell me, how are you faring recently?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Ayato! Wow, so even a busy guy like yourself is here to attend the Irodori Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Preparing festivals falls under the Yashiro Commission's scope of responsibilities. Seeing as Lady Yae has poured her heart and soul into the preparations, I'm obliged to be equally dedicated.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe. Come now Ayato, we're not strangers here. There's no need to sound so formal.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: We were just about to discuss the boards over here. They're related to our little helpers' tasks, so I'll let you give them a detailed rundown.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Certainly. I assume you two already know that the Irodori Festival originated from The Five Kasen. These five boards are here for painting their portraits.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: This Irodori Festival is not only the first major festival to be held in Inazuma since the lifting of the Sakoku Decree, it is also an event deeply rooted in culture and the arts.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Therefore, the Yashiro Commission has personally invited several cultural celebrities from other nations.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: For example, the artist we have invited to paint these portraits hails from the distant land of Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The Yashiro Commission will arrange accommodations and food in Inazuma for each of the distinguished guests. However, we fear that staying in a foreign land may feel a little uncomfortable.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Which is precisely why it would be ideal to have someone familiar with both Inazuma and other nations of Teyvat to serve as a guide for our guests.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I knew you would catch on. It is our hope that you would be able to guide the guests from the harbor to their residence at the International Trade Association while providing any necessary assistance along the way.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This Arrival Schedule includes the details of the ships on which the guests will be arriving. All you simply have to do is go to the docks at the indicated times.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It's settled then. My, look at the time. I have to meet with my editors, so I must be going now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: During the festival, most of the Yae Publishing House's editors will be staying near the Outlander Affairs Agency. If you run into any problems, you may find them there.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This festival requires the full cooperation of the Tri-Commission, and there are still many minor details which require my attention, so I must excuse myself for now. I'll leave the guests in your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the details we need about the ships are on the timetable that Ayato gave us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a closer look and be sure to pick up the passengers according to the times written on it.
